title: How to Rig ANYTHING in Blender!
about: What Lucius kept from this tutorial: one recipe per chapter, each continuing from the scene of the one before. Replay with `lucius teach course courses/Y2SWwZmwrwM` (no API needed).

lessons.title: How Armatures Work
lessons.note: An armature built the tutor's way: a connected chain extruded from one bone plus a disconnected branch; posed in pose mode so the children follow. Shown with bone stand-ins since armatures do not render.

lessons.title: Rigid Rigs
lessons.note: Boxy robot of separate parts, a bone per part (left mirrored), parts parented to bones (Ctrl+P > Bone) and the head via empty groups + assign weight 1; posed.

lessons.title: Let's make a rig
lessons.note: A mannequin mesh (capsule limbs with loop cuts, joints, torso) joined and its transforms applied, and its skeleton the tutor's way: the middle row from the crotch up, one side's chains named .L, mirrored with Symmetrize.

lessons.title: Skin Binding
lessons.note: Parented with automatic weights (Ctrl+P); posed: arm raised out to the side and bent, knee lifted, head tilted -- the mesh bends with the bones.

lessons.title: Weight Painting
lessons.note: Weights fixed from the root up with masks: head, pelvis and chest vertices fully to their bones (auto normalize takes weight from the others).

lessons.title: Constraints
lessons.note: IK legs the tutor's way: disconnected non-deforming IK and pole bones, IK on the shin (chain 2, pole angles adjusted until each knee points at its pole: measured -64/-116), the foot freed and Child Of the IK bone; lifting one IK handle bends that knee straight forward.

lessons.title: Esthetics
lessons.note: IK controls coloured (blue), poles red, the IK-driven thigh and shin bones hidden, so only the controls show.

lessons.title: Drivers
lessons.note: Valve bone X rotation (transform space, the wheel's axle) drives the screw's Z rotation and, divided by two, its height; a cube's Z = sphere one Z - sphere two Z with two variables.

lessons.title: MAKING A FULL RIG
lessons.note: A mechanical bacteriophage modelled as the tutor's stand-in and its skeleton: root in the base, six curved neck bones, head, hip-knee-foot bones for six legs parented to the root, stick display in front.

lessons.title: Binding
lessons.note: Rigid parts parented to their bones, neck tube and rings with automatic weights, head parts to the head bone; tested by bending the neck and raising a leg (cables left behind, as the tutor notes).

lessons.title: Cables
lessons.note: Cables merged, empty groups, root everywhere, each cable's outer part to its leg bone, a half/half band between; the raised leg carries its cable.

lessons.title: Controls
lessons.note: IK handles at the feet and poles above the knees (pole angles set so each leg keeps its rest shape, measured to 0.1 degree like the tutor's eyeballed 180/135), poles follow their handles, root/body split so the body dances with the feet planted, neck IK (chain 7) following the body. Tried: crouch and turn, a foot lifted, the head pulled aside and down.

lessons.title: Cleanup
lessons.note: Deform bones hidden, control shapes (hexagon, circles, pyramids) in a hidden Controls collection assigned as custom shapes, colours by role: root yellow, body green, IK blue, poles red.

lessons.title: Driver Fun
lessons.note: Rope material from a wave texture through a mapping node; the mapping's X location driven by leg one's bones (local Z rotation): -leg + (-knee/10), as the tutor sets it up (he then removes it because all cables share one material).

lessons.title: Overview
lessons.note: The rig animated only through its controls: body bobbing and turning with feet planted, a foot stepping via its IK handle, the head looking around via its IK handle; 73 frames rendered from a camera.
